postureSelectionLaw: policy-backed SELECT-only chosen under the operator's least-privilege mandate: the driver read (getMyDriverBus) runs client-mediated through the user's JWT (requireSupabaseAuth builds the publishable-key client with the bearer token), so RLS applies and the honesty valve 'service-role-mediated, no client policy' does NOT fire; the J-005 tenant-equality shape is NOT expressible on this substrate (no neutral tenant reference column, no bridge from the legacy campus uuid key to neutral tenant refs, and the live neutral membership substrate holds ZERO bindings for real sessions — verified read-only 2026-10-03), and the legacy domain helper predicate class is banned from the policy layer by J-005/J-006 and by the shrink-only neutrality guard; the expressible least-privilege predicate that matches the actual flow is the assignment-identity binding driver_id = auth.uid() — the same sanctioned auth.uid() self-derivation the 20261002000013 grantor pin uses

tables.name: transport_buses
tables.rationale: policy-backed SELECT-only driver self-assignment read (T-D 20261003000041): exactly one policy (transport_buses_select_driver_assigned: FOR SELECT TO authenticated USING (driver_id = auth.uid())) with authenticated granted SELECT and nothing else, FORCE RLS per the battery §2 convention (the table owner holds the sanctioned BYPASSRLS, so definer paths are unaffected), anon/PUBLIC at zero privileges, service_role unchanged as the sanctioned server-only path. The predicate binds the row's own assignment column (the legacy users-table FK) to the server-derived identity: a row is visible only when it names the actor as its assigned operator, so a foreign-campus row cannot become visible unless that campus's own administrators assigned the actor — cross-campus leakage would be a data-integrity defect of the admin surface, not of this read gate. NO write privilege or policy of any kind is granted; every other read family (caregiver tracking, admin fleet surfaces) remains denied pending its own least-privilege authoring

policyScopeDeviation.declared: assignment-identity scope (driver_id = auth.uid()) instead of the J-005 tenant-equality shape
policyScopeDeviation.reason: the legacy table carries no neutral tenant reference (the recorded basis of the H3-040 zero-policy adjudication); the live neutral substrate holds zero membership/assignment bindings for real sessions, so a tenant-equality predicate would deny every real session and restore nothing; the legacy domain helper predicate class is banned from the policy layer (J-005/J-006, shrink-only neutrality guard)
policyScopeDeviation.conversionPath: a full J-005 tenant-scoped conversion must introduce a neutral tenant reference on the substrate plus a campus→tenant bridge and backfill (a substrate conversion owned by a future mission — no schema was invented here); the battery §4.4 data-declared cross-tenant probe recipe CANNOT be declared for this legacy FK-bound table (uuid campus key; probe aux tables are restricted to the cg_ namespace), so the cross-tenant stage is superseded for this entry by the battery's IDENTITY-SCOPED probe stage (declared via probeStage) and the post-apply proof paths are the battery catalog/privilege/anon-deny sections, the live two-principal identity probe, and the driver e2e case
